recentItems.title: UKRAINE STRIKES A DRONE DEAL — New Agreement with Finland as Russia Tries to Save Its Remaining Oil
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian drones continue to strike Russian military and energy infrastructure. Damage to an oil depot was reported in Rostov Region, while a fire broke out at an industrial facility in Krasnodar Krai. Another key topic is the “Crimean Switch Off” operation conducted by Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces. According to Commander Robert Brovdi, over the course of two and a half months, Ukrainian forces targeted 412 energy facilities in Russia and in temporarily occupied territories.

During the night of September 24, Kyiv came under a Russian attack involving ballistic missiles and drones. According to the city authorities, two people were killed and eight others were injured. The damaged sites included a maternity hospital, private homes, warehouses, and vehicles.

Meanwhile, the sixth Crimea Platform Summit took place in New York. It brought together representatives from more than 60 countries. Zelenskyy said that the current level of representation was the broadest in the six years since the format was launched. Participants discussed Crimea, international pressure on Russia, human rights, Black Sea security, and further international steps.

recentItems.title: BIRTH UNDER BALLISTIC ATTACK: Russia’s Massive Strike and Zelenskyy’s Talks on Patriot Systems
recentItems.description:
Russia launched another combined attack on Ukraine using Zircon missiles, ballistic missiles, and 282 drones of various types. According to Ukraine’s Air Force, Ukrainian air defence destroyed or suppressed 227 aerial targets. The main directions of the attack were Kyiv and Odesa regions. People were killed and others were injured in Kyiv during the overnight ballistic attack. Residential and civilian facilities were damaged, including Maternity Hospital No. 2. At the time of the attack, patients and medical staff were sheltering underground — and it was there, at 2:05 a.m., that a baby boy was born.

The Kharkiv, Odesa, Khmelnytskyi, Rivne, and Zhytomyr regions also came under attack. This episode covers the aftermath of the strikes, the situation at the front — where Ukraine’s General Staff recorded 277 combat engagements — as well as attacks by the Defence Forces on two Russian radar stations and a launch site for attack drones. Another key topic is Ukraine’s protection against ballistic missiles. Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Mark Rutte discussed the consequences of Russian strikes and the needs of Ukraine’s air defence.

recentItems.title: “PUTIN IS PATIENT ZERO!” Zelenskyy tears the Kremlin apart at the UN: 248,000 corpses in 8 months!
recentItems.description:
At the UN General Assembly, Volodymyr Zelenskyy called Putin “patient zero,” revealing the catastrophic cost of the war for Russia: 248,964 occupiers lost in eight months of 2026 — 248 lives for every square kilometer seized. Amid Armed Forces of Ukraine strikes, even Donald Trump acknowledged the collapse of Russian oil refining.

Despite massive air terror using ballistic missiles and jet-powered Shaheds, Ukraine has tested four types of its own high-speed interceptors and, together with 10 partners, launched the FREYJA counter-missile program.

The President warned the Kremlin: if Russia strikes our energy infrastructure, “General Winter” will strike Russia itself. He also called on the leaders of 47 states to stop the recruitment of their citizens to be slaughtered for the sake of Moscow’s ambitions.

recentItems.title: Patriots to be produced in Ukraine: Trump positive on licenses, and Russian refineries on fire again
recentItems.description:
Ukraine may get the opportunity to produce interceptor missiles for Patriot systems inside the country. After talks with Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the U.S. president is positive about issuing the necessary licenses, and the Ukrainian side has already discussed cooperation with the manufacturer. According to Zelenskyy, launching production could take about a year to a year and a half. In parallel, Kyiv has proposed a reciprocal energy ceasefire: Ukraine is ready to stop strikes on Russian energy facilities if Moscow halts attacks on Ukrainian ones.

Meanwhile, reports from Samara again mention a fire at the Kuibyshev refinery — a day after a Ukrainian strike. Earlier, hits on AVT-4 and AVT-5 units were reported. The Rosneft-owned plant can process around 7 million tons of oil per year and has repeatedly been targeted by Ukrainian long-range strikes.

The episode also covers Russia’s jet-drone attack on Kyiv, the situation with Russia’s “shadow fleet,” U.S. troops in Poland, and new problems in Russia’s oil sector. India is cutting purchases of Russian oil, while Moscow tries to develop the large-scale Arctic Vostok Oil project and at the same time faces problems in its domestic fuel market.

recentItems.title: ZELENSKYY PROPOSED AN ENERGY TRUCE TO PUTIN — WHAT WILL THE RESPONSE BE?
recentItems.description:
The UN General Assembly is currently underway in New York, where one of the main issues remains ending Russia’s war against Ukraine. Following talks with Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was ready for a reciprocal energy truce: Kyiv is prepared to stop striking Russia’s energy infrastructure, provided that Moscow takes the same step. The United States is expected to convey this proposal to Russia. Zelenskyy also called for Xi Jinping to be involved in the diplomatic process, taking China’s influence over the Kremlin into account.

At the same time, Russia continues its attacks on Ukrainian cities. Kyiv has reported fatalities and dozens of injuries, while residential areas, gas stations, a business center, and railway infrastructure have been damaged. In the Odesa region, a port, a civilian cargo vessel, and warehouses came under attack. In the Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions, Russian strikes damaged residential buildings and other civilian facilities. Over the past 24 hours, 247 combat engagements were recorded along the front line, with particularly intense fighting in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions. At the same time, Ukraine’s Defense Forces are striking Russian UAV control centers, drone and fuel depots, and military logistics facilities. Could an energy truce become the first step toward broader negotiations, and what role do the United States and China play in this process? More details in the episode.
